issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares a Pneumatic interface with a method named openValve(): void, but the solution implements Pneumatic with a method named releaseValve(): void. This method-name/signature mismatch between the specification and the provided solution will confuse students about which method to implement and will cause integration/tests expecting openValve() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method in the solution (and any implementations) from releaseValve() to openValve() to match the UML/problem statement. Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement to use releaseValve() consistently. Ensure LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster implement the same method name declared in Pneumatic.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement and the ride implementations use the method name openValve() for the pneumatic action, but the Solution's Pneumatic interface declares releaseValve() instead. This creates a direct naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (opening/releasing the pneumatic valve) and will confuse students mapping the UML to the code — it also prevents a consistent implementation across interface and classes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic interface method name consistent with the UML and implementations. Rename releaseValve() in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java to openValve(), or alternatively rename all implementing methods (in LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster, and the UML) to releaseValve() so that interface and implementations use the same identifier.
